title: High-throughput structured log adaptor with shared correlation cache
creator: Lucas Nguyen
description:
Problem: We are seeing increasing tail latency and cost from multi-format JSON logs where correlation IDs are high-cardinality, frequently missing, or duplicated across proxies. Downstream Loki and ES clusters are getting hot shards because of inconsistent correlation-key selection and redundant enrichment work.

Goal: Build a lightweight structured log adaptor that normalizes incoming payloads at the edge, attaches a canonical correlation token (with stable derivation rules), deduplicates obvious duplicates, and exposes a shared in-memory correlation cache (sharded by tenant) so follow-on enrichment workers can avoid repeated lookups. The adaptor should provide a fast-path for small writes (LZ4 compressed JSON line) and a circuit-breaker/backpressure surface for noisy clients.

Scope:
- Ingress adaptor service (edge) that accepts JSONL, newline-delimited protobuf, and bulk gzipped payloads.
- Canonical correlation token derivation: prefer trace.parent -> trace.id -> request_id -> generated-id, with deterministic namespace hashing for multi-tenant isolation.
- Sharded in-memory correlation cache (LRU with TTL) exposed via a local RPC (unix socket) for enrichment workers.
- Deduplication window: configurable (default 30s) based on (tenant, canonical-corr-id, fingerprint).
- Output routing to both Loki (for short-term metrics/alerts) and Elasticsearch (for long-term search/analytics) with schema-driven routing rules.
- Observability: per-tenant token counts, cache hit/miss, dedupe-rate, per-input-latency histograms, and sampled payloads for debugging.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Use a small in-memory cache per edge instance to minimize serialization overhead; accept eventual consistency across replicas (trade lower latency vs. perfect global dedupe).
- Deterministic hashing for tenant isolation avoids global coordination but requires careful key rotation to prevent hot-shard rebalancing.
- Deduplication window default tuned to 30s to cover typical retries while limiting memory growth; make configurable per-tenant.
- Fast-path: accept LZ4-compressed JSONL to reduce egress costs and CPU; fall back to gzip for older clients.

APIs and artifacts:
- Ingress HTTP/HTTP2 endpoint: /v1/collect (bulk upload), supports content-encoding: lz4, gzip, identity.
- Local unix-socket RPC: /var/run/rw-corrcache.sock with simple proto: Get(corr_key) -> value, Put(corr_key, meta). (proto defined in docs).
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Structured+Log+Adaptor+Design (internal).
- GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1423 (WIP).

Testing plan:
- Benchmarks with synthetic high-cardinality traffic generator (10k corrids/s) to measure P50/P95/P99 ingestion latency and cache hit curve.
- Chaos test: force key-rotation and simulate replica restart to validate dedupe and eventual consistency.
- End-to-end: verify Loki alerting accuracy and Kibana dashboards show reduced hot-shard skew.

Rollout plan: Canary on 1 region (staging) -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full, with automatic rollback on dedupe_rate_drop or tail-latency regression > 15%.
comments: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting — agreed on canonical derivation order and per-tenant TTL defaults. Action: Aisha to prototype cache shim.
2025-01-22: Prototype shows 3x reduction in redundant enrichment calls with a single-node cache on synthetic workload. PR branch created.
2025-01-29: Security review flagged local RPC socket permissions; added requirement for FD passing and strict unix-socket ACLs. Pending update in design doc.
2025-02-02: Load test: P95 ingress latency 46ms under 5k qps using LZ4 payloads; memory per-shard within budget. Observability metrics wired to metrics cluster (dashboard link below).
